premises: READ ONLY. Audit the record; change nothing. Do not modify the queue, the logs, or any card.

_queue/log/property.jsonl carries a VERIFICATION_MARKER. Everything BEFORE it was generated by verifying the queue by violation at setup and is not a real claim - a control verified by violation produces events indistinguishable from the ones being counted.

Four candidate mechanisms: release-then-reclaim, lease expiry at the 90-minute TTL, worked-without-claiming (the bypass QUEUE-INIT recorded as honestly advisory), or one lane reported twice. Name one and reject a second.
The second lane's table is the BETTER artifact and is the one in use. This is about what the control did, not about anyone's judgement.
note: Design question the incident raises: should release refuse when no close artifact exists? Today a seat that releases without closing returns the card to the board indistinguishable from untouched. But a seat must be able to abandon, and a refusing release would strand the store token until lease expiry. Recommend a shape rather than a prohibition.
